BiblicalUsage: mânôwn is a continuator, an heir, and it occurs once, in Proverbs 29:21. There a servant delicately brought up from a child shall at length become a son. The word is the one who carries the house on after the master.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mânôwn reminds me that how a household is raised decides who inherits it, and that grace can turn a servant into a son.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
